text:
John Carlson's last calendar year took him from Washington to Anaheim late last season and then to Tampa Bay on a two-year deal in free agency. At 36, he is on a strong run: 14 points in his last ten games, including three assists against his old team on Nov. 17.

This one is earned. He has 20 points (7 goals) in 22 games, the Lightning control 60.5% of the 5v5 expected goals with him on the ice, and his own chances are up too. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 6.5 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 93rd percentile among defensemen, and his shot still tops 94 mph by NHL Edge tracking.

The goals are the part to fade: 7 on 4.1 expected, shooting 14% after 9% last season. And the old weakness is still worth watching: All Three Zones had only 31% of his exits keeping possession, so a heavy forecheck can pin him. Our range has him at 54 to 76 points, a big season for a defenseman his age.
